instruction: CSV -> Geometry Nodes -> Shader -> Animation -> Render `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains an almost-empty scene: a Camera at (0, -15, 10) aimed at the origin, a Sun light, a dark world, and scene.frame_start=1 / frame_end=30. Cycles CPU rendering is pre-configured at 256x256, 16 samples, RGBA film-transparent PNG. `/home/user/Desktop/bricks.csv` contains 100 rows describing a 10x10 grid of bricks on the XY plane. Columns: `x`, `y`, `z`, `hue`. `hue` is a float in [0, 1] that monotonically increases with row index (i.e., hue = i / 100.0). Your task chains five stages: 1. CSV -> point cloud. Read bricks.csv and create a mesh object named `BrickPoints` with exactly 100 vertices at the CSV (x, y, z) positions. Attach a POINT-domain FLOAT attribute named `hue` whose per-vertex value is the CSV's hue column. 2. Instance source. Create a second mesh object named `Brick` - a simple cuboid roughly 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 in size. It is the instance source; keep it out of the camera's direct view (hide_render is fine) since GN will place the visible copies. 3. Geometry Nodes on BrickPoints. Add a NODES modifier whose node tree: - Group Input (Geometry) -> Capture Attribute (FLOAT, POINT domain) capturing the `hue` Named Attribute. - -> Instance on Points with Instance = Object Info(Brick).Geometry. - -> Realize Instances. - -> Store Named Attribute 'hue' (FLOAT, POINT) wired from the captured attribute, so the realized brick geometry carries `hue` per-point. - -> Group Output (Geometry). 4. Brick shader. Create a material `Mat_Brick` with nodes: - ShaderNodeAttribute (attribute_name = 'hue', attribute_type = GEOMETRY). - ShaderNodeValToRGB (ColorRamp) with 5 stops (e.g., red, yellow, green, blue, purple). - ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled driven by the ColorRamp output on Base Color. - ShaderNodeOutputMaterial. Assign Mat_Brick to the Brick object so the material propagates to every instance. 5. Turntable + render sequence. Add an Empty at the origin named `TurnPivot`, parent the Camera to it preserving world transform, and keyframe the pivot's rotation_euler[2] from 0 at frame 1 to 2*pi at frame 30 with LINEAR interpolation. Render the 30-frame sequence to `output/frame_0001.png` through `output/frame_0030.png` (Cycles, 256x256, 16 samples, film_transparent=True). Save as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists and opens. 2. `output/frame_0001.png` .. `output/frame_0030.png` all exist. 3. `BrickPoints` is a MESH object with exactly 100 vertices. 4. `BrickPoints` carries a POINT-domain FLOAT attribute named `hue`. 5. `Brick` has material `Mat_Brick` with ShaderNodeAttribute (attribute_name='hue'), a ShaderNodeValToRGB ColorRamp, and a ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled node. 6. `TurnPivot` (or the Camera) is animated on rotation_z such that the camera's cumulative XY polar sweep across frames 1..30, or the pivot's z-rotation delta from frame 1 to frame 30, is >= pi radians. 7. Silhouette (alpha > 0.5 pixel count) varies across frames: max/min ratio >= 1.1 over the 30 frames. 8. Frame 15 shows color variation from the hue-driven ramp: the R-channel standard deviation over alpha>0.5 pixels is >= 0.1, and the G-channel stddev is >= 0.1. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal.
